Is it accurate to state that the computations specified by an artificial neural network can involve more than math because activation functions such as relu involve more than just math?

message.content: No, it is not accurate. Activation functions like ReLU are strictly mathematical operations (e.g., $f(x) = \max(0, x)$). While neural networks model complex systems, their computations remain within the domain of mathematics and logic; they do not inherently involve non-mathematical elements.
